text: The two acceptance operations are fixed as POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/offer-acceptances on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, declared in capability area Case record with right C for the POST and right R for the GET and with scope applied, and the caller is the self-service channel (LINE OA, HOME.SCB) through the gateway-bff route with its own identity and the customer's session. The case stage on rwb-case, the contact point and its consent on rwb-source-data and the contact stop on rwb-deviation are consumed as fakes until their published operations exist.
why: No source names an acceptance operation, a customer role or a right for a customer-facing tap, and the legacy permission check names Litigation C and R, which is the module template's copy; the plan declares no C row on the three consumed rows and the app story cannot start without them.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-036 sections 12, 13 and 16; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.15 and A2.15.3.3; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; Ownership Map via the P6 context pack; Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R9
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead, the rwb-access owner and the gateway-bff owner confirm the capability area, the two rights and the caller identity when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: The channel calls one path per operation through the edge; a customer role that later enters the permission matrix needs no change to the app story, only a row in the contract story and in the fake.

text: The customer's acceptance is recorded as one local decision record against the notice and the case, relayed on the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 by the library, and the case and the treatment act on it from that record; this service publishes no event, holds no acceptance state and writes no case fact.
why: The catalogue holds NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered for this service and no acceptance event, and DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, so an event cannot be declared without inventing a topic element and a consumer.
read: Architecture v5 slide 42 event list; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03 applied, DP-09 not applied); ADR-022; FSD P6 A2.15 step 3
confirm: The rwb-decision owner and the rwb-comms tech lead confirm that the case reads the acceptance from the ledger in the strict mode of the record when the contract is baselined.
impact: The acceptance reaches the case with the same latency as any recorded decision; a consumer that expects a comms acceptance event would need a new catalogue row and a delta story.

text: The decision code and the rule of an acceptance are the columns of the routing row in force, read from the stage code of the case: D5 or D6 with R-RES-16 for OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER, D6.4 with R-SET-10 for OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET, and D6.4 with R-DIL-18 or R-DIL-19 for OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_DIL. The mapping of a stage code to a decision code and a rule is a versioned configuration row of the service and never a constant.
why: The routing table gives the decision set and the rule per route and per event but no single code for an acceptance, and no source names the mapping table the service would read.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16, R-SET-10, R-DIL-18 and R-DIL-19; FSD P6 A2.15; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03)
confirm: The rwb-decision owner confirms the decision sets and the rule versions that an acceptance carries when the decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is baselined.
impact: A change of a route's decision code is a configuration change with a new version and not a code change; an unmapped stage refuses the tap.

text: A repeat of the acceptance with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first answer and writes no second decision; a second acceptance of the same notice with a different key is refused with 409 and writes no second decision; and an unavailable consumed answer or an unavailable decision record answers 503 with the platform error envelope.
why: The legacy table names no message and no status for a second acceptance and the platform envelope is the only error shape the services use; the idempotence rule of the platform and BR12 forbid a second decision for one notice.
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s17 and R8; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.2 (Idempotency-Key on writes); legacy RWB-E4-036 message table
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead and the API review confirm the status and the text of the second-acceptance refusal when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: A customer who taps twice sees one acceptance; a channel that retries with a new key receives a refusal it must show, which is the safer of the two outcomes.

text: FEAT-COM-02 is traced to its feature, its rules and its routing rows and not to a requirement ID, because the P6 requirement list stops at REQ-OCC-011 for FEAT-COM-01 and holds no row for FEAT-COM-02.
why: The P6 requirement table of TSD P6 T8 has no row for the feature, and a traceability section cannot cite a requirement that no source defines.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T8; FSD P6 Communications v3 A1.2 and A2.15; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row E4 / P6 / FEAT-COM-02
confirm: The requirement owner of the Epic 4 BRD adds a requirement row for FEAT-COM-02 at the next revision.
impact: The RTM carries this key under the feature and the rules until a requirement ID exists; no test case and no criterion changes when it is added.

text: The two acceptance operations are fixed by the contract baseline as POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/offer-acceptances on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, with a closed request of noticeId and channel, a closed answer of eight elements, Idempotency-Key on the POST only, capability area Case record with rights C and R, and the two unnamed refusal texts carried as placeholders until the baseline review fixes them.
why: No source names either operation, its request, its answer, its errors or its right, and the app story needs one fixed contract on Day 1.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1, T-A.2 and T6.1; FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.15 and A2.15.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-036 message table; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R7.2 s12
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead, the solution architect and the rwb-access owner confirm the paths, the rights and the two refusal texts at the baseline review.
impact: The channel and the case record call two paths on one base; a change of a path is a new major version and a rewrite of both consumers.

text: The three consumed elements of the baseline are the case read that carries the stage code on rwb-case, the contact point of a party with its consent and verified flag on rwb-source-data, and the open deviations of a case on rwb-deviation; each is declared as consumed, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and faked, because the plan declares no C row on any of them.
why: The capability cannot apply the two conduct rules or the stage check without those three answers, and no C row exists for them in this key.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4 and R5.5 (DP-05); Ownership Map via the P6 context pack; FSD P6 A2.15 integration points; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-RES-19, R-SET-12 and R-UNI-10
confirm: The rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-deviation owners publish the three operations; until then the fakes answer the document and the drift test keeps them true.
impact: The app story runs end to end against fakes from Day 1; the integration of the three real answers moves to an ITG story and blocks no build.

text: The baseline declares no acceptance table, no acceptance column, no acceptance event of rwb-comms, no workflow and no Schedule, and no offer amount, validity date, acceptance state or consent state in any schema, example or fake; the acceptance is the decision record and the three notice events are not repurposed.
why: The catalogue holds three events for the service and none for an acceptance, DP-09 and DP-10 are not in the pattern set of the key, and the offer value, the validity and the consent are other owners' data.
read: Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Template and Rules v1 R5.5; Ownership Map via the P6 context pack; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (offer validity of R-RES-11 and R-SET-06)
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead and the platform owner confirm the negative declarations at the baseline review; the absence tests keep them.
impact: The service holds no offer data and no acceptance state, so a later request for an acceptance event or a report of acceptances is a delta story and not a change to this baseline.
